subject.title: Bug: isRecurringTopOfHourCronExpr fails to match cron expressions with step values

question: Should maintainers adopt the open fork PR, replace it with a maintainer-owned narrow fix, or close that linked fix path before repair work continues?
rationale: Current main and the latest release still have the bug, but the issue is already paired with an unmerged non-maintainer-editable fork PR, so automation should not open a competing fix without maintainer direction.

options.title: Replace with maintainer-owned narrow fix
options.body: Open or land a small OpenClaw-owned PR that implements Croner-compatible minute-zero detection and regression coverage, then close the fork path as superseded.

options.title: Adopt the fork PR
options.body: Ask a maintainer to take over or recreate the open fork PR so it can be reviewed, proven, and merged under OpenClaw's normal branch controls.

options.title: Decline the semantic expansion
options.body: Close the issue and linked fix attempts if maintainers decide the shipped contract should remain literal minute `0` only.

recommendation.title: Replace with maintainer-owned narrow fix
recommendation.body: Open or land a small OpenClaw-owned PR that implements Croner-compatible minute-zero detection and regression coverage, then close the fork path as superseded.

likelyOwner.reason: The default stagger behavior appears to have been introduced in steipete's commit `c26cf6aa830c739e009e93d6b44162407ea1fb25`, making this the strongest routing signal for the maintainer choice.
